newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Fifty percent of Austrians expect soft euro.
newsitem.headline: Fifty percent of Austrians expect soft euro.

text.p: Around 50 percent of Austrians expect the planned single currency euro to be softer than the schilling, a survey by market research institute IMAS showed on Friday.
Just seven percent of those questioned believe the euro will be harder than the schilling.
Some 42 percent expect the single currency to have a negative effect on their personal situation, while just seven thought it would bring positive benefits.
"The mistrust of the forthcoming currency is deep-seated and almost indiscriminate through all cross sections of the population," IMAS said in a statement.

IMAS said 22 percent of those surveyed felt they had a good grasp of the single currency issue. Some 46 percent did not think they were very well-informed while 23 percent felt they were "not at all well-informed".
People who were more familiar with the issue were not necessarily more likely to be less sceptical about the introduction of the euro, IMAS noted.
Austria joined the European Union and its exchange rate mechanism in January 1995 after more than two-thirds of Austrians voted in favour of membership in a referendum.
